# Results — Study 193 (Window-Dressing) on real SPY daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The recipe: label each
trading day as a **pump day** (one of the last 5 trading days of a calendar quarter:
Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec) or a **reversal day** (one of the first 5 trading days of the next
quarter). The Carhart et al. (2002) claim predicts pump days earn more than baseline
(mutual-fund window dressing bids up winners) and reversal days earn less (mechanical
unwind). We test this on **SPY daily total-return prices** and a random-day placebo.
As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n days | n pump | n reversal | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| SPY total return (`SPY_total_return.parquet`) | 1993-02-01 to 2026-06-12 | 8,399 | 670 | 669 | `3e185e607be5` |

## The three tests

### Test 1: Pump window (last 5 days of each quarter) vs baseline

| Group | n | mean (bps/day) | HAC t | Welch p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Pump window** | 670 | **+1.69** | **+0.48** | **0.554** |
| Other days (baseline) | 7,060 | +3.78 | — | — |
| **Contrast (pump − other)** | — | **−2.60** | — | **0.635** |

- The pump window earns **+1.69 bps/day** — actually *below* the baseline of **+3.78 bps/day**
  (contrast = **−2.60 bps**, Welch p = 0.635). The Carhart hypothesis predicts a positive
  contrast; we observe a slightly negative one. Statistically invisible: HAC t = **+0.48**.
- There is no evidence of fund-driven quarter-end price inflation in SPY over 1993–2026.

### Test 2: Reversal window (first 5 days of next quarter) vs baseline

| Group | n | mean (bps/day) | HAC t | Welch p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Reversal window** | 669 | **+9.61** | **+2.16** | **0.214** |
| Other days (baseline) | 7,060 | +3.78 | — | — |
| **Contrast (reversal − other)** | — | **+6.01** | — | **0.230** |

- The reversal window is **above** baseline by +6.01 bps/day — the opposite sign of what the
  Carhart reversal story predicts. The HAC t = **+2.16** on the reversal returns in isolation
  partly reflects the strong equity risk premium and is not a signal of window-dressing reversal.
  Welch p against baseline = 0.214 — not significant after Bonferroni correction (see below).

### Test 3: Long-pump / short-reversal spread vs random-day placebo

| Arm | n active days | mean (bps/day) | HAC t | ann. return |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Long-pump / short-reversal** | 1,339 | **−3.96** | **−1.39** | **−10.0%/yr** |
| Random-day placebo (seed 193) | 1,339 | +0.66 | +0.23 | — |

- The spread strategy (long on the last 5 days of each quarter, short on the first 5 of the
  next) earns **−3.96 bps/day** at HAC t = **−1.39** — not significant, and negative.
- The random-day control earns essentially zero (+0.66 bps, t = 0.23), confirming the equity
  premium is priced out on active days. The calendar timing adds **−4.62 bps/day vs the coin**.
- No break-even trading cost exists: the gross spread is negative.

## Multiple-comparisons window sweep (windows 1–10 days)

Sweeping the window from 1 to 10 days: the most extreme individual p-value is 0.019
(reversal at window = 1 day), but after Bonferroni correction for 10 window choices the
corrected p = 0.193 — nowhere near significance.

| window | contrast pump (bps) | p pump | contrast reversal (bps) | p reversal | p Bonferroni |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | −7.44 | 0.397 | +24.90 | 0.019 | 0.193 |
| 2 | −8.44 | 0.225 | +15.45 | 0.044 | 0.443 |
| 3 | −6.54 | 0.241 | +11.02 | 0.065 | 0.653 |
| 4 | −2.95 | 0.543 | +9.70 | 0.076 | 0.757 |
| 5 | −2.60 | 0.554 | +5.99 | 0.215 | 1.000 |
| 6–10 | (all p > 0.08) | — | (all p > 0.25) | — | (all p > 0.32) |

All Bonferroni-corrected p-values exceed 0.19 — the sweep does not surface a significant
window at conventional levels.

## Sub-period stability

| Period | pump mean (bps) | reversal mean (bps) | other (bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1993–2009 | −0.6 | +7.5 | +2.8 |
| 2010–2026 | +4.0 | +11.8 | +4.8 |

The pattern is broadly consistent across both sub-periods: pump near or below baseline,
reversal above baseline. This is the **opposite** of the textbook Carhart story.

## Synthetic positive control

On a deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_daily`) with a planted `wd_effect`,
the same engine recovers the pump-and-reversal spread monotonically: the strategy earns
a strong positive spread only when the effect is planted, and earns approximately zero
on a null tape (wd_effect = 0). This confirms the machinery works — the real tape simply
has no detectable window-dressing signal to harvest.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Pump contrast = −2.60 bps (Welch p = 0.635); spread HAC t = −1.39;
  all Bonferroni-corrected window sweep p-values exceed 0.19. The textbook pump is absent;
  the reversal runs in the wrong direction.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The gross spread is negative (−3.96 bps/day) and the strategy
  trades ~40 days per year, making any positive round-trip cost add to a loser.
- **Quarter-end behaviour: inverted.** On SPY since 1993 the last days of the quarter are
  slightly *below* baseline and the first days of the next quarter are slightly *above* — the
  opposite of the classical window-dressing story. Neither contrast is statistically significant.
